body: Nomad Investment Partnership with Qais Zakaria (2001-2013/14): ~921% cumulative vs ~117% for MSCI World; ~20.8% a year net per one source vs ~6.5% for the index. Closed and returned capital in 2014 because they felt the work was done; partnership letters are public and widely studied. Early book: deep value in Asia/UK small caps; it evolved into a very concentrated portfolio of Amazon, Costco and Berkshire Hathaway (a German source says ~3 stocks at the end; uncorroborated). Process edge: 'destination analysis' - what will this business look like in 10-20 years - and the 'scale economies shared' model: firms that pass scale savings back to customers (Costco's low markups, Amazon's prices and free shipping) grow volume, which creates more scale savings, a flywheel competitors cannot match. Structural edge: an LP base and fee structure (performance fee over a hurdle, with deferral/clawback features - details unverified) that let them hold for a decade. Mistakes: Sleep wrote about errors of commission in early deep-value holdings and errors of omission (not sizing winners up sooner) - specifics unverified. Copyable: look for Indian companies that deliberately price low to widen the moat (DMart-style retail, low-cost brokers, platform businesses), judge them on customer value per rupee, and hold through quarterly noise.
title: Nick Sleep - Nomad and 'scale economies shared'
